correctness.rationale: Away from Y=0 smoothness follows from the nonzero partial derivative in Y; along Y=0 the four branch roots are simple, including the unique rational point at infinity. A smooth plane quartic has genus three. I recounted all 33 extension counts independently in F13 and the fields with u²=2 and u³=2 (base-field root tests certify these moduli), using precomputed norms of each linear factor and the norm-cubed quartic residue test. All three counts in all six rows matched. The Newton recurrence plus genus-three reciprocity gave six distinct full numerators, each matching the stated trace triple. Explicit nonsingular y²=x³+Ax+B witnesses for traces (−6,−4,−2,2,4,6) used (A,B)=(1,0),(1,1),(0,5),(0,1),(2,0),(2,1); Tate's theorem gives the asserted base-field isogenies. Listing the six anharmonic transforms verified the three stated orbits, each with two polynomials. Fractional-linear changes preserve the branch configuration, but a scalar fourth-power class matters for the marked equations; 28 versus 4 at 4 and 10 precludes their arithmetic isomorphism.
residual_risks: Exhaustion only of the eleven F13 parameters of the marked pencil. No claim to classify unmarked quartics or all twists in a geometric class.

value.rationale: Characteristic 13 is the first prime field with both fourth roots of unity and nontrivial cubic roots of unity, so both the quartic residue classes and the equianharmonic orbit occur. A complete computation there separates arithmetic isogeny information from the classical geometric branch quotient in all three orbit types, including a 24-point spread within a single orbit. The exact spectra and coalescences in this natural small field are useful independent of a general higher-prime theorem.
residual_risks: No generalization of the particular six-type pattern to other characteristics or fields is inferred.
